title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to section 9° 'Récapitulation sur le cas universel' of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' notes, a sequel to La Longue Marche. In the preceding pages Grothendieck works with the profinite completion of the modular group and its automorphisms.

Notation, as best reconstructed:
- G = GL2(Z), G^+ = SL2(Z), with hats denoting profinite completions.
- σ (order 4) and ρ (order 6) are the standard elliptic elements.
- L_σ ≅ Z/4 and L_ρ ≅ Z/6 are their centralizers in SL2(Z)^.
- π is the profinite completion of the level-2 congruence kernel, i.e. Ker(Ĝ → S_3) after adjoining ±1. π_0 is a complement isomorphic to the free profinite group on two generators, so π = π_0 × μ with μ = {±1}.
- M is a universal group of automorphisms. It contains Ĝ^+ (acting through the adjoint action) as a normal subgroup, with quotient an extended Galois-type group Π_Q~ (the tilde version of the arithmetic fundamental group Π_Q).
- γ_{ρ,σ} is the group introduced earlier as the solution group of the loop ('lacets') equations attached to the pair (ρ,σ).

Statement (a)(3): the group 𝔐_{ρ,σ} built from the pair (ρ,σ) is isomorphic to the universal group M.

Statement (4)/(4bis): the morphism of extensions
  1 → L_0 → Z_{ρ,σ} → γ_{ρ,σ} → 1
  inside
  1 → Ĝ^+_{ρ,σ} → G_{ρ,σ} → γ_{ρ,σ} → 1
is identified with
  1 → L_0^G → M[*] = M(0)·L_0^G → Π_Q~ → 1
  inside
  1 → Ĝ^+ → M → Π_Q~ → 1.
In particular γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ Π_Q~.

Statement (5)/(5bis): the characters of γ_{ρ,σ} correspond to characters of Π_Q~:
- the cyclotomic character χ: Π_Q~ → Ẑ*;
- two maps Ẑ* → μ;
- the composites ε_3 and ε_2: Π_Q~ → μ.
These are reductions of χ modulo 6 and modulo 4 respectively, since (Z/4)* = (Z/6)* = μ.

Part (b): the 'normalizer' of σ is
  N_σ* = {u ∈ M | u(σ) = σ^{ε_2(u)}},
where the exponent makes sense because σ has order 4. Equivalently u(σ) = ε_2[τ](σ), where τ (or τ') is an orientation-reversing involution in GL2(Z)^ conjugating σ to σ^{-1}.

Intersections (7):
- N_σ* ∩ Ĝ = D_σ = {1,τ}·L_σ, a dihedral group of order 8;
- N_σ* ∩ Ĝ^+ = L_σ ≅ Z/4;
- N_σ* ∩ π = μ;
- N_σ* ∩ π_0 = {1}.

Purpose: the next page uses these intersections to show that M(1/2) := N_σ* ∩ M_0^! maps isomorphically onto γ_{ρ,σ}. This gives semidirect product splittings M^! ≅ M(1/2)·π, M_0^! ≅ M(1/2)·π_0, etc. In other words, the Galois-type quotient is lifted by normalizing a chosen elliptic element of order 4, much as GT elements are normalized on the generators of B_3/center ≅ PSL2(Z). Part (c), on the next page, does the same for ρ with Z/6.
errors: The first row of diagram (4) has a middle term that should be Z_{ρ,σ}. This is consistent with the previous page, Z_{ρ,σ} ≅ M(0)·L_0^G = M[0], and with the overbrace M(0)·L_0^G in (4bis). It is not Γ_{ρ,σ}.

Formula (6) leaves unclear whether the exponent is ε_2(u) or -ε_2(u); a crossed-out ε_1 is replaced. Because ε_2 takes values in {±1} this is only a sign convention, but the convention is not fixed on the page.

The page is a recapitulation; no proofs are given here. The intersection claims are plausible: σ has finite order, so its centralizer in the free profinite group π_0 is trivial, and its centralizer in Ĝ^+ is L_σ ≅ Z/4.

ideas.what: Identification of the abstractly defined group γ_{ρ,σ} (solutions of the loop equations for elliptic elements ρ, σ) with an extended arithmetic fundamental group Π_Q~, via an isomorphism of extensions with kernel profinite SL2(Z)
ideas.modern_name: Galois/GT action on profinite SL2(Z) = Γ_{1,1}^, and B_3/center; GT^ variants defined via the modular group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1997, GT acting on Γ_{1,1}^), Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto for the elliptic/genus-1 setting
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the modular tower and the Galois action on profinite SL2(Z) in general terms only

ideas.what: Normalizer of a torsion (elliptic) element twisted by the cyclotomic character mod 4 or mod 6, giving a section of M → Π_Q~ and semidirect product decompositions
ideas.modern_name: Normalized lifts/sections of the outer Galois action fixing inertia generators at elliptic points (cf. Ihara's normalization of GT elements by fixing x up to x^λ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Drinfeld (normalization of GT), Nakamura for the PSL2 setting

ideas.what: Intersections of the normalizer with Ĝ, Ĝ^+, π, π_0: dihedral of order 8, Z/4, μ, trivial
ideas.modern_name: Centralizers of torsion elements in profinite modular / free profinite groups

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a 'universal case' in which the Galois-type group is recovered as a normalizer of an order-4 elliptic element inside the automorphism group of profinite GL2(Z), using the characters ε_2 and ε_3 (cyclotomic mod 4 and mod 6). This is close to, but phrased differently from, the later Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps 'new version of GT' built from SL2(Z) data. The precise dihedral/character bookkeeping (D_σ, L_σ, ε_2, ε_3) is a variant not obviously recorded in the literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an alternative characterization of GT-type groups via elliptic normalizers in the profinite modular group. This is relevant to comparisons between GT^ and the genus-one/modular versions. The idea is largely anticipated by LNS 1997.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished, systematic treatment of the Galois action on profinite SL2(Z)/GL2(Z) through normalizers of elliptic elements, predating similar published work (Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps). However, it is a recapitulation of known-style structure, and the core idea is now in the literature.
transcription_corrections: The first row of (4): 'Γ_{ρ,σ}' should read 'Z_{ρ,σ}'.
In (5bis) the upper curved arrow Π_Q~ → μ is labelled ε_3, not ε_1; the lower one is ε_2. The diagram is Π_Q~ →χ Ẑ* followed by two maps Ẑ* → μ.
In (5) the labels read ε'_ρ = ε^ρ_1 (upper arrow) and ε''_ρ = ε^ρ_2 (lower arrow), crossed and overwritten.
The top line 'C — ∘' is a fragmentary heading/continuation mark of item (a), not a formula.
The next page's number '515' is presumably 622.
